grammar.title: Reflexive Verbs in Italian
grammar.explanation: Reflexive verbs in Italian end in -si in the infinitive (svegliarsi, vestirsi, alzarsi) and use reflexive pronouns: mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si. The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb: 'mi sveglio' (I wake up), 'ti vesti' (you get dressed). In the infinitive, the pronoun attaches to the end after dropping the final -e: 'devo alzarmi' (I have to get up). Reflexive verbs use 'essere' in compound tenses: 'mi sono svegliato/a' (I woke up).
